correctness.rationale: Fourier character eigenvalues follow from an exact rank-one two-step convolution identity. A rigorous pairwise comparison uniquely maximizes the powered-distance spectrum at rank m-1 for all p>0. An explicit positive factorization proves a root in (0,1), strict convexity gives uniqueness, and the exact finite-field rank count gives the endpoint Euclidean dimension. Exhaustive binary 4-by-4 Fourier checks and parameter-root checks independently corroborate.

evidence: The prior three-column uncapped rank-metric result has rank diameter three; it cannot contain rank-four differences. Delsarte (1978) proves the Fourier eigenmatrix, without the weighted sharp sign optimization.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Transposition identifies the old three-column case with 3-by-n, whereas the claim assumes m>=4. An inclusion of the old space in a higher-rank space gives only an upper bound on admissible exponents, not equality nor a complete endpoint shell. The stated proof establishes both directions and exact multiplicity; the old result is not reclassified as new.
